 OKANOGAN, Wash. — Authorities have identified the pedestrian killed in a hit-and-run collision early Sunday morning in Okanogan as Albert Comeslast of Omak, a Native American and member of the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation.
 The Okanogan County Coroner's Office confirmed Comeslast's identity and determined that he died from blunt force trauma to the head and torso.
 The fatal collision occurred at approximately 2:30 a.m. on November 15, 2026, along State Route 215 in Okanogan.
 According to the Okanogan County Sheriff's Office, Comeslast was struck by a vehicle whose driver fled the scene following the collision.
 Investigators have now confirmed that the vehicle continued southbound on State Route 215, also known as Elmway, toward the city of Okanogan. Authorities are asking residents and businesses along that route to help identify the driver.
 The Sheriff's Office has issued a public request for surveillance footage from homes and businesses along SR 215 and surrounding streets.
 Residents are specifically being asked to review security cameras, doorbell cameras and dash cameras for footage recorded around 2:30 a.m. Sunday, including the minutes before and after the fatal collision.
 Investigators hope the footage will help identify the vehicle involved or establish its movements after the driver left the scene.
 Authorities have not released a description of the suspect vehicle or identified the person believed to have been driving.
 The Okanogan County Sheriff's Office is leading the investigation, with assistance from the Washington State Patrol, Omak Police Department and Colville Tribal Police Department.
 Authorities have not disclosed the circumstances leading up to the collision, including whether Comeslast was crossing the roadway or walking alongside it when he was struck.
 The identification of Comeslast marks a significant development in the investigation as authorities continue working to determine who was responsible for the deadly collision.
 The Okanogan County Sheriff's Office has extended its condolences to Comeslast's family and loved ones.
 Anyone living or operating a business along SR 215, Elmway or nearby streets who has camera footage from the early morning hours of November 15 is urged to review it, even if the footage does not directly show the collision. 
 Anyone who witnessed the crash, recognizes a potentially involved vehicle or has information that could assist investigators is encouraged to contact the Okanogan County Sheriff's Office at (509) 422-7200 .
 The investigation remains ongoing, and no arrests have been announced.
